Mutable reference
Borrowing helps you reuse values safely, without giving them away.

1. It lets you use values without taking ownership
2. It avoids cloning, which can be slow for large data
3. It makes your programs safer and faster

Unnamed: 2:
Mutable references (&mut T):
1. Only one mutable reference can exist at a time.
2. While the mutable reference exists: The owner cannot be used, No other mutable or immutable references can exist.
3. When the mutable reference goes out of scope, the owner becomes unlocked, and new references can be created.
-> Guarantees exclusive, safe mutation without data races (Multiple writes can cause conflict in many circumstances)

Immutable references (&T):
1. Any number of immutable references can exist at the same time.
2. While immutable references exist: The owner can be read but not mutated, You cannot create a mutable reference at the same time.
-> Allows multiple read-only accesses safely (Multiple reads do not conflict, so it’s safe to allow as many as you want)
